achievements.description: You welcomed the sprite and received its blessing.
You navigated the twisting corridors of the Great Maze and emerged on the other side with your wits-and your sneakers-intact. Not even a dead end could stop you.

nodes.text: The forest seems normal. Goblins, bugs, and fairies roam the forest. Nothing out of the ordinary. The forest is still lit by the sun - probably because it's high noon and the trees, so far, are normal.

{WAIT=1}
A sprite lands on my shoulder. Rumors say these sprites have been blessed, and their touch can grant blessings or take them away from me. {COLOR=#FFDB51}Should I shoo it away?{ENDCOLOR}
The sprite left. Seemingly unagitated by my skeptical attitude towards it.
{COLOR=#66FF00}I checked my stats with an appraisal to find out that my Mana regenerates by 1-20% after each battle.{ENDCOLOR}

I've been documenting the species I've come across, and so far, these life forms can be relocated to a nearby ecosystem outside the forest. The forest was indeed teeming with life. A few meters after the sprite encounter, I saw {COLOR=RED}a bloodied hobgoblin{ENDCOLOR}. Hobgoblins are considered the bottom of the food chain. However, its left hand was cut off - not with a bite mark, but a sweeping cut, seemingly of a sword. {COLOR=#FFDB51}Should I help him?{ENDCOLOR}

{COLOR=#66FF00}I battle the goblin's seeming perpetrator. I won and aided the goblin. I used one of my potions to heal it.{ENDCOLOR}
{COLOR=RED}[[-1 Potion]{ENDCOLOR}
I dont think this is part of my job. I dont want the hobgoblins' perpetrators to be after me. I turned a blind eye to the creature and continued venturing.

As I ventured further, all of a sudden, I felt a tree branch stop me in my tracks. I thought I stumbled on a branch, but I couldn't lift my foot as the branch completely wrapped around my foot. I looked back and saw a tree with a pattern of a face. {COLOR=#FFDB51}Is this what they call a Treant?{ENDCOLOR}{WAIT=1}

The sun starts setting after a couple of meters of walking. Honestly, my legs are getting tired. Luckily, {COLOR=#66FF00}I heard a stream nearby{ENDCOLOR}, which I immediately chased after. I set up camp and sent a letter to the capital through my letter bird. Attached to the letter are the creatures I came across today. I've used one of my food packs for dinner tonight before casting a barrier cloak to protect my camp and leave it invisible. I've settled into my spot in my sleeping bag and dozed off without any issues. {WAIT=2}

achievements.description: Better safe than sorry, I suppose...
Take a leap of faith into unexplored territories.
You take your final breath assessing the choices you made.

nodes.text: I've been awakened by {SHAKE}faint rustling{ENDSHAKE} outside the camp. {WAIT=1}I did not fear for my safety as my barrier still stands. I peeked outside my sleeping bag to see {COLOR=RED}Salamanders{ENDCOLOR} drinking from the stream. Normally, {COLOR=RED}salamanders{ENDCOLOR} are found in swamps. Quite interesting how these {COLOR=RED}salamanders{ENDCOLOR} are {SICK}green and not red{ENDSICK}. Their spine is much more protruded, and their eyes shut from side-to-side. Had I not known anything, I'd say they were {COLOR=RED}baby dragons{ENDCOLOR}. After drinking from the stream, {WAVE}they swam along its flow{ENDWAVE}. Truly a curious creature indeed. They'll make my notes for sure. I'm starting to think that maybe {COLOR=RED}this forest should be left alone{ENDCOLOR}.
I packed my belongings and dispelled the cloak. I have some space left in my bag for water. {COLOR=#FFDB51}Should I bring some from this stream?{ENDCOLOR}

{COLOR=#66FF00}I packed 10 bottles just in case. I don't know whether to feel glad that I found a stream this early or be scared that I might not find another place to get water. I packed water to fill the remaining space in my bag. Better safe than sorry.{ENDCOLOR}
This forest won't survive if this stream is the only water source this place has. I'd better save some space, or when I need it.

As the adventure pushed through, the trees became much taller and wider. The forest looked dimmer, so I started etching lines on trees to mark the places I've been to. The bushes start thickening and growing higher. {COLOR=#FFDB51}What should I do?{ENDCOLOR}

choices.label: CUT THE BUSHES IN FRONT OF YOU WITH A SPELL
COMB THROUGH THE BUSHES WITH YOUR HANDS

nodes.text: I cast a spell to clear the bushes in front of me. Luckily, I went with my gut and chopped out these bushes, or else I would've fallen into this {SHAKE}{COLOR=RED}cavern{ENDCOLOR}{ENDSHAKE}. If this forest is to be cleared out, the kingdom should send an expedition team. Caverns are not suited for research mages such as I.
{COLOR=RED}Your blind steps brought you harm. You fell into a ravine with no way back to the surface except the way you fell in. You take 4 damage.{ENDCOLOR}

I am stuck here with no light whatsoever except the light from the {COLOR=RED}sinkhole{ENDCOLOR} I fell in. My breaths echoed, which only meant one thing - this {COLOR=RED}ravine{ENDCOLOR} is wide enough for me to explore.

I kept walking straight ahead, hoping for my eyes to adjust in the darkness. After a while, I see {COLOR=RED}a faint glow{ENDCOLOR} in the distance. {RAINBOW}Bioluminescent moss{ENDRAINBOW} covered the walls of this cave. I ran towards it.
{COLOR=RED}You tripped. You take 2 damage.{ENDCOLOR}

I inspected the {RAINBOW}bioluminescent moss{ENDRAINBOW}. It was rare to me as I do not fall into caves often, nor do I voluntarily explore them. {WAVE}Water dripped on my shoulder{ENDWAVE}. It doesn't feel like normal water. I looked up to see where it came from.
nodes.label: {COLOR=#FFDB51}TAKE A SECOND TO OBSERVE{ENDCOLOR}

nodes.text: {COLOR=#66FF00}A cavern creature with glowing eyes was drooling. You managed to strike it first before it could lunge.{ENDCOLOR}
{COLOR=RED}A cavern creature with glowing eyes was drooling. It lunges at you and takes the first turn.{ENDCOLOR}

I defeated the creature. The creature that was so unique, I would've never imagined could exist. A creature so {RAINBOW}extraordinary{ENDRAINBOW} that my curiosity skyrocketed through the roof. I have to find more about this place.

As I venture deeper, the {RAINBOW}luminescent moss{ENDRAINBOW} starts thickening — gradually lighting this once dark abyss. Flowers that look like corals crawl across the floor and upward the walls. However, what shocked me was these {WAVE}fish-like creatures{ENDWAVE}, hovering as if they were swimming.
nodes.label: {COLOR=#FFDB51}FEEL THE MAGIC OF THIS PLACE{ENDCOLOR}

nodes.text: {COLOR=#66FF00}Magic fills the place{ENDCOLOR}. You see {RAINBOW}Mana traces{ENDRAINBOW} so thick, it stuns you momentarily. Abusing the stun, a {COLOR=RED}centipede-like creature with gills{ENDCOLOR} snarl at you and attacks you.
Your sensation to mana does not connect in this place. Something might be blocking this connection.

I've lost track of time - and quite honestly, my mission too. There's only one goal in my mind right now - to find the light of day or the shine of the moon. Although, I'd be lying if I say that the {RAINBOW}beauty of this place{ENDRAINBOW} does not mesmerize me.

After a couple steps, I hear {SHAKE}a terrifying scream{ENDSHAKE} - not of a human, but of a beast. I don't know whether to be glad or scared as I remember this war cry. It was of a {COLOR=RED}Leviathan{ENDCOLOR}. {COLOR=RED}Leviathans{ENDCOLOR} normally inhabit deep sea trenches but the cavern lacks the size to handle it. However, I was mistaken. After taking a left at a place resembling a crossroad, the already large ravine just changed the game. A deep, and wide cliff reveals itself to me. The cliff was so deep and wide that a {SHAKE}{COLOR=RED}large lava pool{ENDCOLOR}{ENDSHAKE} engulfs the majority of this cavern's floor. I look up and I see the {COLOR=RED}Leviathan{ENDCOLOR} hovering over the lava pool.
{COLOR=#66FF00}You managed to reach the ravine floor without issue.{ENDCOLOR}
{COLOR=RED}You fall into the ravine as your step gets heavy by mistake. You take 5 damage.{ENDCOLOR}

The cavern floor was hard to traverse; some rocks were unstable to walk on. I make sure that I check for stability before standing on a platform or else I meet my end. The {COLOR=RED}Leviathan{ENDCOLOR} screeches once more, the {SHAKE}whole cavern shakes{ENDSHAKE}, and I luckily dodge the stalagmites that fall. However, unlike me, another {COLOR=RED}territorial Leviathan{ENDCOLOR} was unlucky. The second Leviathan engaged in combat with the first one, causing {COLOR=RED}fireballs{ENDCOLOR} to rain from the sky. Each fireball that hits the terrain unleashes a minor earthquake, enough to crack the platforms beneath me.

Barely making it alive, I escaped the {COLOR=RED}hellrain{ENDCOLOR}, and the second leviathan was subdued. A fireball revealed {RAINBOW}a hidden section{ENDRAINBOW} of the cave. The entrance of the section was… {SHAKE}pulsing{ENDSHAKE}. I ventured into the entrance. This section was even deeper than this lava-filled terrain I am in. Oddly enough, this section has no Lava at all. I hear {WAVE}a faint sound, similar that of a chime{ENDWAVE}. When I looked back, the cavern's entrance closed as if it was never opened.
{BOUNCY}"{RAINBOW}Save me from the steel of the steed{ENDRAINBOW}"{ENDBOUNCY} A voice echoed directly in my head.
nodes.label: {COLOR=#FFDB51}TAKE A SECOND TO OBSERVE{ENDCOLOR}

nodes.text: Your eyes quickly adjust in the darkness and lock eyes with a spherical mass of soil, root, and moss.
"Protect me from the flames, young one." You hear once again. The cavern then glows for every syllable you heard.
{SHAKE}"What are you? Who are you?"{ENDSHAKE} I shout, hoping to reveal whoever it was that spoke to me.
{WAVE}"The soil breathes, the trees listen. The sky hears, and the creatures watch over. I am the place you stand on. My breath is the air you live on. My blood is your sustenance."{ENDWAVE}
I do not understand its poems, but its intentions were clear. It was the cavern - no, the forest speaks to me.
Lights emit from the core of the cave. This sphere - resembling an egg - speaks to me in ways I cannot fathom.
{BOUNCY}"{RAINBOW}Save me from the steel of the steed.{ENDRAINBOW}"{ENDBOUNCY} The core repeated again and again. The cave was pulsing, and the "heart" seemed to be beating.
"What do you mean?" I ask.
Before the heart could react, I saw the {COLOR=RED}knights of Drakeswood{ENDCOLOR}, in full armor, line up at another one of the cavern's entrances.

choices.label: ASK THEIR BUSINESS WITH THE CAVE

nodes.text: The knights aim their weapons at you. They tell you you know too much. {COLOR=RED}10 knights attack you.{ENDCOLOR}{WAIT=2}

{COLOR=RED}They say you've been gone for a month. Drakeswood believes that the forest has absorbed you as its food. However, they do not want you to know that to eliminate the forest was their true goal. Without hesitation, their captain swings at you. A fierce boss battle starts. The heart does not help you on this one.{ENDCOLOR}

{COLOR=#66FF00}I won the fight, leaving the knights' bodies on the ground.{ENDCOLOR} The cave absorbs them for nutrients - even those who were still breathing. The forest takes, the forest survives. It fights for itself and chooses the righteous ones to help itself. I ask the forest to let me go to notify Drakeswood of its "existence".
Whether I succeed or don't, I shall return to this forest and guard it.{WAIT=3}

The expedition went on as expected until I was greeted with a local hobgoblin settlement. A campfire is set ablaze in the middle of this settlement, with these goblins dancing around it. I've been told that this is a ritual to choose another hobgoblin chief. Should I..?
Hobgoblins are docile creatures; they won't attack unless I agitate them with combat. I entered the settlement to observe. Research is research anyway.
I'd better stay here. I don't think I should get involved with local customs.
Bandits rush the gate. With a quick, wide glance you counted five bandits in a V-formation with their seeming squad leader speaking:
"Bring me your newly elected chief!" In fluent hobgoblin dialect.
I don't know what to do. These hobgoblins just had their chief elected. These poor creatures are being harassed by these bandits! I should…
I tried talking them out. These bandits must have an agenda. I sure hope they do not intend anything bad.
I injured the bandit leader and saved the hobgoblins from the trouble. I went near to his heavily wounded body to finish what I started. Under his breath, he said his final words:
"You should not have meddled."

I investigate the camp that the goblins evacuated. It seems like these hobgoblins are more civilized than I thought. They use cooking ware like pots and pans. They use tools like they're second nature to them. I explored the village further and noticed a church-like structure. It was mostly decorated with stones with various paintings and colors. I'm starting to see an interesting pattern here in the forest.

I kept staring at this smoke pillar. I am beyond curious on what I'll encounter. If there's something I always liked with this job, it's the uncertainty. The sun had started to set which told me I have to start walking.
The closer I get, the more torches I notice. Whatever this place is, it's a civilized one.

There are smoke pillars near here, seemingly from another settlement. I took the time to venture into it. A path was seemingly made towards it. Without a second thought, I followed it. The path led me to a wooden gate with two towers on each side. Beside each tower is a wall, studded with torches. I approached the gate and was met by a voice.
"State your name and name your business."
It was the voice of a hobgoblin and… in their dialect. It seems I have been deeply affected by that spore. I can now understand hobgoblins, I guess. I just hope it's permanent. Should I?
"I am a harmless researcher. I would like to enter this gate."
The hobgoblin jumps from his tower and lands in front of me. The creature is clothed in heavy metal armor. It held its spear in front of me with obvious intent to kill.
"Prove it." the hobgoblin snarled.
How should I prove it?

choices.label: DROP YOUR WEAPONS AND RAISE YOUR HANDS

nodes.text: Without any second thoughts, you killed the guard. The other watchtower's hobgoblin sounded the gong. Shocked with what you've done, your knees shake as an army of hobgoblin warriors make chase to you riding their giant bullfrogs. Should I?

choices.label: FIGHT THE BULLFROG SOLDIERS FROM AFAR
CAST A SPELL ON YOURSELF TO ESCAPE THE MOB

nodes.text: You casted a spell in an attempt to thin down the soldiers making chase as you, yourself, run with haste.

The bullfrogs are coated with magic-resisting bodily fluids. The attack fizzles out and enrages the bullfrogs. It leaps and crushes your spine. The hobgoblins loot your belongings and your dying corpse was left by the soldiers to rot.
You take your final breath assessing the choices you made.
The spell succeeds but the watchtower's mage casted an invisible barrier, that traps you several meters outside the gates. You slam in it, head first. Ending your life in a quick, gruesome death.
The guard picks your weapon up and hands it to you. The gates open and a neatly dressed hobgoblin welcomes you to the city.

The city is wide and bright. Torches light the place up and the pillars of every building in the city are made of gold. The hobgoblins treat me with a warm welcome with everyone waving and bowing to me. These hobgoblins are way more civilized and smart from those hobgoblins in other places. I could not ask for more. My hobgoblin companion asked me to join their dinner. They guided me to their meal hall where every single hobgoblin eats together. The doors of the hall opened and I was met with the Hobgoblin King. The hall was then silent as the king stood and walked in front of me.
He was towering and intimidating. His cape is what you would expect a royal would have. Grand, big, and red. His staff was studded with gold. Which, in hobgoblin culture, meant high status.
"Welcome! Short Shaman!" The king screamed with a voice of welcoming excitement. "I am Schakh O'yanezoon and we welcome you to our country!"
"Treat this Short Shaman as one of us! For a visitor is rare to come!"

The hall rejoiced and hobgoblins servants placed plates for every seat in the hall with equal portions. What weirds me out is that though I am taller than every hobgoblin here, I am referred to as a Short Shaman. Regardless, I enjoy my meal along with the citizens of this hobgoblin city.
After a luxurious dinner, the king invited me to his throne room. I believe he has sensed that I come with a purpose. I am in luck as I needed his presence for this concern.

"My king. I am here with a purpose." I pleaded. "A nearby kingdom sends me to study this forest - which I believe is your dominion. This kingdom wants to put you in its border or demolish this forest. I want your blessing and opinions on what I should do."

Shocked by the fact that you can understand hobgoblins and skeptical whether these creatures can understand you, you leave the gates and march around the settlement.  As you traverse around the walled city, you finally understand how large the place really is. Two hours of walking just got you around the west gate of the city.
